messages.author: f4c3467fbe3bbbec
messages.subject: Oddly small openCR density estimates
parts:
Hi All,

I am trying to estimate density for a population of woylies inside a predator-free fence. The data spans over 10 years (with 15 sessions). The woylies are caught using standard cage traps. For the first five sessions, transects with each trap 200m apart were used, and for the subsequent 10 sessions 9x9 grids with 25m spacings were used. Each session is a separate trapfile (as there was varying effort throughout).

I have run the model as a closed population in SECR which gives me fairly reasonable density estimates however I would like to try open population as woylies can live quite long (up to 8 years). The SECR density estimates are between 0.1 and 2.8. When I run a JSSAsecrD model in openCR (with exactly the same data files and mask), the density estimates for the first five sessions (transects) are similar, but the density estimates for the subsequent 10 sessions are very odd (e.g. 7.342360e-28). I tried running only the grid data (sessions 5-15) and I still get these unreasonably small estimates.

Does anyone have any idea why these estimates might be so tiny? I have copied and pasted my two codes below with the respective predictions.

Any insights would be greatly appreciated!
Cheers,

Tash

sanctuary_capthist <- read.capthist(captfile="openCR_PerupSanctuary_captfile.txt

                trapfile = list("trapfile_session1.txt",

                                "trapfile_session2.txt",

                                "trapfile_session3.txt",

                                "trapfile_session4.txt",

                                "trapfile_session5.txt",

                                "trapfile_session6.txt",

                                "trapfile_session7.txt",

                                "trapfile_session8.txt",

                                "trapfile_session9.txt",

                                "trapfile_session13.txt",

                                "trapfile_session14.txt",

                                "trapfile_session15.txt"),                                   

detector = "multi",  #mothers can have joeys in same trap

                                    fmt=c("trapID"),

                                    trapcovnames="Design",

                                    noccasions = 4)

 

intervals(sanctuary_capthistGRID)<-c(5,12,13,5,7,12,11,13,12)/12             

PSmaskGRID<-make.mask(traps=traps(sanctuary_capthistGRID),  # a shapefile of the fence

                  buffer=400,

                  spacing=50

                  poly=PSfence,

                  poly.habitat=TRUE)

 

## SECR model

secr_base <- secr.fit (sanctuary_capthist, mask=PSmask,

                               buffer = 800,

                               trace = FALSE,

                               CL=FALSE,

                               model = list(D~session,g0~session,sigma~session),

                               detectfn = "HR",

                       ncores=4)

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Oddly small openCR density estimates
parts:
Why not be happy with the closed estimates?

We could troubleshoot what is wrong with your open model (all ~t certainly too ambitious) and data (not shown but presumably thin in parts), but really use of openCR requires that you are willing to troubleshoot for yourself and own the unpleasantness that open models often bring.

On Thursday, December 9, 2021 at 8:59:38 PM UTC+13 tash.d....@gmail.com wrote:

Hi All,

I am trying to estimate density for a population of woylies inside a predator-free fence. The data spans over 10 years (with 15 sessions). The woylies are caught using standard cage traps. For the first five sessions, transects with each trap 200m apart were used, and for the subsequent 10 sessions 9x9 grids with 25m spacings were used. Each session is a separate trapfile (as there was varying effort throughout).

I have run the model as a closed population in SECR which gives me fairly reasonable density estimates however I would like to try open population as woylies can live quite long (up to 8 years). The SECR density estimates are between 0.1 and 2.8. When I run a JSSAsecrD model in openCR (with exactly the same data files and mask), the density estimates for the first five sessions (transects) are similar, but the density estimates for the subsequent 10 sessions are very odd (e.g. 7.342360e-28). I tried running only the grid data (sessions 5-15) and I still get these unreasonably small estimates.

Does anyone have any idea why these estimates might be so tiny? I have copied and pasted my two codes below with the respective predictions.

Any insights would be greatly appreciated!
Cheers,

Tash

sanctuary_capthist <- read.capthist(captfile="openCR_PerupSanctuary_captfile.txt

                trapfile = list("trapfile_session1.txt",

                                "trapfile_session2.txt",
